gallery.title: File:376bombgroup-bulgaria-01-jun-1944.gif
gallery.description:
USAAF 376th Bombardment Group over Sofia, Bulgaria, after an attack on the city.  In the lower left Wolf Stadium can be seen along with Lake Ariana and a racetrack.  Possibly taken 17 April 1944.  Originally identified as a picture of a 456th Bombardment Group B-24, the markings on the aircraft are those for the 376th.
United States Army Air Forces photograph via US National Archives
categories: 376th Bombardment Group (United States Army Air Forces)
Bombing of Sofia in World War II

gallery.title: File:Bronze coin of Serdi Celts.jpg
gallery.description:
Serdi region
187-168 BC or later
obverse: right-facing head of the river god Strymon (the modern Struma River)
reverse: wide trident
ref: type: (A?)5B
imitation of: SNG Copenhagen 1298-9 var.
weight: 8,37g
diameter 22-20mm
This coin is overstrike of official Thessalonican coin:
Thessalonica
187-31 BC
obverse: head of Dionysos with ivy wreath right
goat standing right
ΘEΣΣA_ΛO / N_IK_HΣ
(NE) / ? other monograms
Sear #1466; BMC Macedonia p. 110, 10 - 16

Imitation coins from the Serdi region weren't meant to fool Macedonian traders as counterfeit but were minted as their own currency. This coin, an overstrike on a coin issued by a Macedonian authority, is evidence of this emulative and transformative purpose.

gallery.filename: Bulgaria Bulgaria-0546 - Church of St Nicholas the Miracle-Maker (7390227698).jpg
gallery.title: File:Bulgaria Bulgaria-0546 - Church of St Nicholas the Miracle-Maker (7390227698).jpg
gallery.credit: Bulgaria-0546 - Church of St Nicholas the Miracle-Maker
gallery.source: Bulgaria Bulgaria-0546 - Church of St Nicholas the Miracle-Maker (7390227698)
gallery.description:
Church of St Nicholas the Miracle-Maker, was built on the site of the Saray Mosque, which was destroyed in 1882, after the liberation of Bulgaria by Russia from the Ottoman Empire. The five domes are coated with gold. The bells were donated by Emperor Nicholas II.
Construction began in 1907 and the church was consecrated in 1914.
